english.title: Possess an unlicensed instrument other than a rod and line with intent to use it for fishing
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in a place, namely **(..SPECIFY PLACE..), in which fishing for fish by a licensable means of fishing, namely **(..SPECIFY MEANS OF FISHING..), was regulated by a system of licensing, possessed **(..SPECIFY ITEM IN POSSESSION..), with intent to use it for that purpose when not entitled to do so by virtue of a fishing licence
english.legislation: Contrary to section 27(1)(b) of, and Schedule 4 to, the Salmon and Freshwater Fisheries Act 1975.

english.notes: Paragraph 2 of Part II of Schedule 4 to the Salmon and Freshwater Fisheries Act 1975 provides that any offence against this Act committed on the sea-coast or at sea beyond the ordinary jurisdiction of a court of summary jurisdiction shall be deemed to have been committed in any place abutting on that sea-coast or adjoining that sea, and may be tried and punished accordingly.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a statutory maximum fine.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
